clinician.trajectory_summary: A 65-year-old man with a history of diabetes, hypertension, and recent COVID-19 presented with acute-onset dysphagia, nasal intonation, mild bifacial weakness, decreased palatal movements, and poor pharyngeal reflex. Initial workup included a normal MRI of the brain and spinal cord, NCS showing mild sensory neuropathy, high SARS-CoV-2 IgG titres, and no thymic hyperplasia or thymoma on HRCT thorax. On day 8 of admission, he developed neck and respiratory muscle weakness, with a single breath count of eight and type II respiratory failure (PCo2 52 mm Hg). He was intubated and connected to a ventilator due to a myasthenic crisis. Serum anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody (AchR) titres were elevated at 4.5 nmol/L. Treatment included stopping pyridostigmine, increasing prednisolone to 40 mg/day, and intravenous immunoglobulin (0.4 mg/kg/day) for five consecutive days.
